slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 14:18: Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine—since he was priest of God Most High—
slides.body: “Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine—since he was priest of God Most High—”
slides.heading: Gen 14:18

slides.alt_text: Slide one introduces the claim connecting Melchizedek's priesthood with Jesus.
slides.body: Genesis introduces Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High. Hebrews says Jesus became a high priest forever ‘in the order of Melchizedek.’
slides.heading: Did Genesis predict Jesus's priesthood?

slides.alt_text: Slide two presents the canonical Christian trajectory from Genesis through Psalm 110 to Hebrews.
slides.body: Genesis supplies an unusual priest-king. Psalm 110 promises a royal priest forever in his order. Hebrews explicitly applies that promise to Jesus, whose priesthood depends on indestructible life—not Levitical ancestry.
slides.heading: The strongest Christian case

slides.alt_text: Slide three explains that the predictive element comes from Psalm 110 rather than Genesis.
slides.body: Genesis narrates a priest already serving; it contains no verbal forecast. The future oath and ‘order of Melchizedek’ come from Psalm 110:4. Hebrews builds a serious typology from both texts, but the prediction is not in Genesis 14:18.
slides.heading: A strong type—but note the source

title: Did Genesis predict Jesus as a Melchizedek priest?
